description: Vitamin A (retinol). Potent anti-aging ingredient. Converts to retinoic acid in skin.

efficacies.mechanism: Converted intracellularly to retinoic acid; binds RAR/RXR nuclear receptors, normalises keratinocyte turnover and reduces wrinkle depth. Meta-analytic evidence supports clinical efficacy across multiple RCTs.
efficacies.magnitude: -44% fine wrinkle depth at 24 weeks (0.4% retinol)
efficacies.notes: Kafi et al. JAAD 2007 — 0.4% retinol applied 3x/week vs vehicle.

efficacies.mechanism: Upregulates COL1A1 / COL3A1 transcription via RAR-γ signalling and induces pro-collagen I synthesis in photoaged dermis.
Induces dermal pro-collagen production in long-term cohort follow-up of retinol-treated photoaged subjects.
Thickens viable epidermis and reorganises dermal collagen architecture, improving clinical firmness scores.

skinTypeProfiles.reason: Strong anti-aging benefit; pair with emollients to offset retinoid dryness.
Gold-standard anti-aging active; well tolerated at 0.1-0.5%.
Comedolytic + anti-aging; ideal for photoaged seborrheic skin.
High irritation potential — erythema, peeling, and barrier disruption common in reactive skin. Prefer bakuchiol or HPR alternatives.
Anti-comedogenic; ramp slowly to avoid retinoid dermatitis.

incompatibilities.reason: Benzoyl peroxide is a strong oxidiser that chemically degrades the retinoid backbone when co-applied; the retinoid + BPO + light combination drives rapid oxidative inactivation of the retinoid, blunting its efficacy. Demonstrated for tretinoin (>50% degradation in ~2 h, ~95% in 24 h under light); retinol is converted along the same retinoic-acid pathway and shares the oxidation-prone polyene structure.
incompatibilities.mitigation: Apply at separate times of day (e.g. retinoid PM, BPO AM) or on alternating days. Adapalene is the BPO-stable retinoid if a same-routine combination is required.
